cases.purpose: A msgbox on an 80x24 PTY draws the title, the text and an OK button; the screen edges stay blank; the terminal is in raw/no-echo mode while the box is open.
cases.oracle: dialog(1) widget conventions (exit 0 OK/Yes, 1 No/Cancel, 255 Esc; result strings to stderr by default; arrow/Tab/space/Enter navigation). The dialog program is not installed in the reference image, so the reference side runs the dialog-compatible whiptail(1) 0.52.25 from the reference PATH with the same widget arguments (candidate: the dialog builtin). Screen contents decoded independently by pyte. Layout and glyph differences between the two implementations are not asserted.
cases.comparison: Decoded screen rows must contain the title, text and a button labelled Ok/OK; rows 0 and 23 blank; ICANON and ECHO cleared during the widget; status 0 and empty result on both builds.
cases.candidate_script: dialog --title 'Greeting' --msgbox 'Hello from the box' 8 30 2>res; echo "rc=$?" > rc
cases.reference_script: whiptail --title 'Greeting' --msgbox 'Hello from the box' 8 30 2>res; echo "rc=$?" > rc

cases.purpose: After SIGWINCH shrinks the terminal from 24x80 to 14x50, dialog recenters the 8x30 msgbox in the shadow-reserved area and redraws before the next key. The prompt moves from row 8, column 24 to row 3, column 9.
cases.oracle: dialog(1) 1.3 centers a box in the area left after its default shadow (SLINES = LINES - 1, SCOLS = COLS - 2) and prints the prompt on the first interior row. An 8x30 msgbox is therefore at row 8, column 24 on 24x80 and at row 3, column 9 after SIGWINCH to 14x50. The base image has no dialog binary, so this geometry is a candidate contract. The widget must redraw when SIGWINCH arrives, before the next key. Screen contents are decoded by pyte.
cases.comparison: On 24x80 the left border of the prompt row is the first non-space at column 24 of row 8. After SIGWINCH to 14x50, and before Enter, that border is the first non-space at column 9 of row 3. Status 0 and an empty result.
